name: DoorDash
key_signal: DASH trades below its 200-day SMA ($195.4) with a still-negative MACD histogram (-1.04) even as 21-day momentum has turned positive (+8.3%), reflecting a stock caught between a broken long-term uptrend and a short-term bounce off the 52-week low ($143.3).
thesis: Revenue growth of 33% remains robust and gross margins (51.8%) are healthy, while the collapse in trailing P/E (86.9x) to forward P/E (23.7x) signals the market expects a sharp earnings inflection as DoorDash scales its newer verticals (grocery, international, advertising) and operating leverage kicks in (operating margin already positive at 5.3%, FCF of $2.3B). The stock is down ~35% from its 52-week high of $285.5 and has bounced off $143.3, with 21-day (+8.3%) and 63-day (+2.7%) momentum both positive and RSI at a neutral 53.7 — consistent with a name that has been de-risked on valuation while consensus among all 42 covering analysts remains a 'buy.' A reclaim of the 200-day SMA (~$195, roughly 6% above spot) would confirm trend repair.
bear_case: Earnings growth is actually negative (-6.1%) despite the 33% top-line growth, meaning DoorDash is buying growth at the expense of near-term profitability just as its stock trades below its 200-day moving average with a negative MACD histogram — a technical setup consistent with a name still in a downtrend, not a completed bottom. With 42 analysts already covering the stock and a 'buy' consensus baked in, there is limited room for a positive surprise to move the stock further than sentiment already reflects, while a beta of 1.78 and 49% annualized volatility mean any disappointment on the margin-expansion narrative (the entire bull case behind the 23.7x forward multiple) could quickly reprice the stock back toward its $143 low, especially since the 126-day momentum of -13.6% shows the broader trend is still deteriorating.
